stories.headline: iPhone Duo launch day: lines form outside Apple Stores worldwide, but walk-in stock is limited
stories.summary: Apple’s first foldable iPhone went on sale at Apple Stores around the world on Friday, and lines formed overnight from Shanghai to Chicago and Las Vegas, where one reader counted 30 to 40 people at 4:15 a.m. and more than 150 by opening. Apple had warned that in-store inventory would be “limited,” and that appears to be true: store workers are telling disappointed walk-in shoppers to check the Apple Store app Saturday at 10 a.m. ET for new stock. CEO John Ternus marked the launch at the Domain Northside store in Austin, Texas, with retail chief Deirdre O’Brien, the same weekend the city hosts the Formula 1 U.S. Grand Prix that Apple streams in the U.S. Marketing chief Greg Joswiak celebrated at the Fifth Avenue store in New York. The same morning, 9to5Mac reported, Apple passed Nvidia to become the world’s most valuable company.

stories.headline: Two former FBI officials are charged with lying to Congress about their roles in the Hunter Biden laptop probes
stories.summary: The Justice Department has charged two former FBI intelligence officials, Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides, with lying to Congress about their involvement in the bureau’s investigations of Hunter Biden, including matters tied to his laptop. Both surrendered on arrest warrants Friday and made a first appearance in federal court in Washington. Prosecutors say they have evidence Benavides discussed the laptop story with others inside the FBI, even though he testified that he learned about it from Wikipedia, and that Floris discussed Hunter Biden with members of the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force despite testifying otherwise. “When senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them,” said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro. Floris’s lawyers called her a patriot and the charges “nonsense,” filed “on the eve of an election.”

stories.headline: Gunmen open fire on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Jordan, killing at least six Christians
stories.summary: Gunmen stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud, in Jordan’s Karak governorate, during a funeral on Friday, killing at least six people and wounding 28 in a rare attack on Christians in the mostly Sunni Muslim kingdom. Authorities said the attackers got out of a vehicle and fired on the funeral procession; state TV footage showed two men with pistols and a third with a long gun charging toward the church. A witness said they fired continuously for about five minutes before fleeing, with 150 to 200 people in and around the church, most of the victims between 50 and 70. A manhunt is under way. King Abdullah II vowed the “harshest retaliation,” saying, “We will strike with an iron fist against those who dare to threaten our nation.” Karak, about 110 miles south of Amman, has a significant Christian community.

stories.headline: Melania Trump brokers a ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky so civilians can get aid and evacuate, the White House says
stories.summary: The White House announced Friday that first lady Melania Trump has brokered an upcoming ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the war-ravaged city of Oleshky, so humanitarian aid can get in and civilians can be evacuated. It said she started the talks and that she and a representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leaders on the terms; Kyiv Independent later reported both sides had agreed. Oleshky, on the Dnipro River across from Ukrainian lines, was taken by Russia on the first day of the 2022 invasion and flooded in 2023 when the Kakhovka Dam collapsed. Residents have gone months without electricity, heat, running water or steady food and medicine, roads out are mined and drones patrol overhead, and Ukraine had repeatedly asked for a local ceasefire. The first lady has made children caught in the war a signature issue and has written to Vladimir Putin about reuniting displaced kids with their families.

stories.headline: Breece Hall is questionable and Adonai Mitchell is set to return as the Jets host the winless Dolphins
stories.summary: The Jets could have two key playmakers back for Sunday’s home game against the Dolphins. Head coach Aaron Glenn said wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, who has practiced all week after missing four games with a finger injury, is on track to play and will be a full participant Friday. Running back Breece Hall returned to practice Thursday as a limited participant and will work again Friday, but he will be listed as questionable with the quad injury that has kept him out of the last two games. Guard Dylan Parham (knee) is also questionable. Offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion) and linebackers Kiko Mauigoa (quad) and Joseph Ossai (ankle) are out. The 2-4 Jets have been fully healthy for only a few plays this season, but Geno Smith is completing 69% of his passes and Garrett Wilson leads the AFC with 35 catches.

stories.headline: Tesla cancels the Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand nearly seven years after taking deposits
stories.summary: Tesla has emailed Cybertruck reservation holders in Australia and New Zealand to say the truck won’t be coming. “After careful consideration, plans to produce Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand have been discontinued,” the email says, adding that reservations will be cancelled and deposits refunded within 30 days. Australians began putting down A$150 in November 2019. As a consolation, Tesla is offering a free year of FSD (Supervised) to anyone who orders a Model 3 or Model Y instead. The main obstacle is that the Cybertruck is built only in left-hand drive, while Australia, New Zealand, the U.K. and Japan need right-hand drive, and Australia has its own certification rules. Electrek estimates Cybertruck sales at 7,000 to 8,000 last quarter, about a 30,000-a-year pace, and argues the volumes can’t justify re-engineering the truck. Its overseas launches so far have all been in left-hand-drive markets.

stories.headline: Justice Department opens a Second Amendment probe into gun-permit delays in Waterbury and Middletown, Connecticut
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department has opened an investigation into how the Waterbury and Middletown police departments handle firearm permit applications, looking at whether the two Connecticut cities make residents wait too long and put an unnecessary burden on applicants. Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon framed the inquiry around the constitutional right of law-abiding Americans to bear arms for self-defense. The announcement did not say how many applications are pending or how long the delays have been, and neither city has commented. It is part of a broader federal push on permitting: DOJ is also investigating “egregious and unjust delays” in Pennsauken, New Jersey, and has sued Minnesota over its 30-day waiting period and permit-to-purchase rules. A state audit has separately found that Connecticut’s Board of Firearms Permit Examiners, which hears appeals of pistol permit denials and revocations, built up a backlog of more than 1,200 cases.

stories.headline: Billy Corgan says his Christian faith is why he stands by his 30-year friendship with Marilyn Manson
stories.summary: Smashing Pumpkins frontman Billy Corgan has explained why he has stayed friends with Marilyn Manson through the sexual assault allegations and lawsuits the singer has faced since 2021. Asked on a podcast how he decides who stays in his life, Corgan said, “As a Christian person … you have to stand by your friends. But that doesn’t mean you don’t have an opinion, and that doesn’t mean you’re not critical.” He noted that the Los Angeles district attorney looked at the case for years and declined to press charges, citing statute-of-limitations issues, and said he knew things behind the scenes that are not public. “I personally didn’t feel that he was guilty,” Corgan said. “I don’t want the world to tell me who my friends are and who I should associate with.” Manson, who denies all the accusations, has settled two suits and faces a jury trial in November 2027 in a case brought by his former assistant.

stories.headline: Babylon Bee: NFL to paint “Allahu Akbar” in the end zone for its first game in Paris
stories.summary: The Babylon Bee imagines the NFL swapping its usual end-zone slogans like “Inspire Change” and “End Racism” for “Allahu Akbar” at its first-ever game in Paris, between the Steelers and the Saints, “to accommodate modern French sensibilities.” A fictional league spokesman explains, “We really want to make a good impression on our hosts. … Also, we don’t want to get bombed by terrorists.” The satire jabs at the security worries about playing in Paris “while the city is on fire,” with officials assuring the league the protests are “just about student affordability concerns and nothing else.” It ends with the NFL installing minarets on top of the stadium so the call to prayer can be heard during a “very French halftime show.”

stories.headline: Israel orders a full West Bank closure after soldiers kill two gunmen behind an attack near Hebron
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men the military says opened fire near Yehuda Junction, outside Hebron, on Friday morning. At least five people were wounded, some critically, and responders said shooting was still going on when they arrived. The army said the gunmen carried an M16 rifle and a handgun and that it had stopped a “terror attack against Israeli civilians.” Hours later, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office told security forces to cordon off Hebron right away and prepare to fully close the West Bank starting Friday. After an emergency Security Cabinet meeting, Netanyahu blamed Hamas, saying it was “planning a major attack aimed at murdering innocent civilians.” The army also said it carried out dozens of raids overnight and detained dozens of people linked to Hamas and Islamic Jihad. The attack comes four days before Tuesday’s Israeli election.

stories.headline: Trump calls LeBron James a “total disgrace” and demands an apology for warming up during the anthem
stories.summary: President Trump on Thursday called on LeBron James to apologize after video showed the 76ers star moving his arms and practicing shooting motions while the national anthem was sung before Philadelphia’s season opener against the Knicks on Tuesday. Trump posted the footage on Truth Social and wrote, “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE.” He added that James “should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” James was standing in line with his teammates as singer Avery Wilson performed “The Star-Spangled Banner.” Some social media users backed Trump and said one of the NBA’s biggest stars should set a better example.

stories.headline: Utah man who allegedly posted “I wanna blow up a synagogue” is indicted after six pipe bombs are found in his home
stories.summary: A federal grand jury in Utah has indicted Skyler AJ Rose, 22, of Ogden, on charges including attempting to commit a hate crime, threatening to destroy a building with an explosive and possessing an unregistered destructive device. Prosecutors say that on Dec. 23, 2025, he made several threatening social media posts, including “I wanna blow up a synagogue,” and that investigators traced them to his home’s IP address. The FBI and Ogden police then searched the house and say they found six improvised pipe bombs and one inert device, explosive precursors, two rifles with magazines and ammunition, and a phone showing he had searched online for a nearby synagogue in November 2025. “These alleged threats were identified and stopped before anyone was harmed,” said U.S. Attorney Melissa Holyoak, who warned that anyone who targets a place of worship “will face the full force of the federal government.”

stories.headline: Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk reveals he has Parkinson’s disease at 53
stories.summary: NFL Hall of Fame running back Marshall Faulk, now head coach at Southern University, says he has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. He revealed it on the Caring Neurologist podcast, saying he first noticed stiffness in his hand while playing golf, even when he was not under match pressure, and asked his doctor about it at one of the physicals he gets twice a year. Faulk said medication has eased his symptoms. He still has some rigidity and small tremors, and he watches his gait and balance, but he said things have not gotten worse. “I don’t look at it as something that’s terminal,” he said. “There’s far worse things out there.” Over 12 seasons with the Colts and Rams, Faulk ran for 12,279 yards, caught passes for 6,875 more and scored 136 touchdowns.

stories.headline: The iPod turns 25: Steve Jobs put “1,000 songs in your pocket” on Oct. 23, 2001
stories.summary: Friday marks 25 years since Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPod at a small press event in the Town Hall auditorium at Apple’s Infinite Loop campus. The $399 player had a 5GB hard drive, a monochrome screen, a mechanical scroll wheel and up to 10 hours of battery life, and it needed a Mac running iTunes. FireWire both charged it and synced music fast enough to copy a whole CD in under 10 seconds. Reaction was mixed at first, and MacRumors readers at the time called it overpriced and “far from revolutionary.” It went on sale Nov. 10, 2001, and was followed in quick succession by a touch-sensitive wheel, the 30-pin Dock Connector in 2003 and a color screen in 2004, before going on to help push Apple well beyond the Mac.

stories.headline: PetaPixel reviews the $2,199 Sigma FP2, a tiny full-frame “brick” with a much better sensor
stories.summary: PetaPixel’s reviewer admits he has disliked every Sigma camera body he has tested, but says the new $2,199 FP2 may change his mind. It keeps the brick-like shape and still has no mechanical shutter, but a new full-frame, partially stacked 24-megapixel sensor makes up for much of that, and image quality and autofocus are described as excellent. The body is even smaller than before and weighs 470 grams with battery and card. A new battery raises the rating to 370 shots, and the 2.1-million-dot rear screen now tilts for waist-level and overhead shooting. The camera is covered in 1/4-20 threads for grips and video rigs and is highly customizable. The main complaint is that it has only one front command dial and a rotating D-pad, which made it easy to bump into the wrong setting.

stories.headline: Country Music Hall of Famer John Anderson, the voice of “Swingin’” and “Seminole Wind,” dies at 71
stories.summary: Country singer John Anderson, a member of both the Country Music Hall of Fame and the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame, has died at 71. His family said he was “the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely.” Born in Apopka, Florida, Anderson started out loving rock guitar, citing the Rolling Stones and Jimi Hendrix, then moved to Nashville after high school and worked on the Grand Ole Opry’s roof before he ever played on its stage. He signed with Warner Bros., had his first hit in 1977, opened for Merle Haggard and became one of the leading New Traditionalists with “1959,” “Wild & Blue,” “Swingin’” and later “Seminole Wind.” In recent years he worked with Dan Auerbach. Blake Shelton wrote that he saw Anderson last Sunday and told him he loved him: “This one really hurts.”

stories.headline: Warhound, backed by Colossal and Palmer Luckey, raises $200 million to gene-edit and clone military working dogs
stories.summary: A new startup called Warhound has raised $200 million to genetically engineer working dogs for the U.S. military, police and first responders and equip them with gear designed by Palmer Luckey’s Anduril. It was created by Colossal Biosciences CEO Ben Lamm, whose company is behind the dire wolf “de-extinction” claims, and Luckey. Warhound has collected cell samples from top-performing U.S. working dogs, mostly Belgian Malinois plus some Labradors and shepherds, and has started editing their genes before cloning them. The first goal is fewer breed-related problems such as hip dysplasia and some cancers. Later edits could target speed, agility or a stronger sense of smell for bomb detection. Anduril will design goggles, vests, body armor and software. About 80% of U.S. military dogs now come from Europe, and the first engineered pups are expected in early 2027.

stories.headline: Musk says a NASA panel’s estimate of 22 Starship launches per Moon landing is “way too high”
stories.summary: At NASA’s Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel meeting on Thursday, former astronaut Charlie Precourt flagged in-orbit refueling of SpaceX’s Starship lunar lander as a major risk for Artemis IV, the mission planned to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028. “I think the last estimate is around 22 flights,” he said. After Ars Technica’s Eric Berger posted the comment on X, Elon Musk replied, “That’s way too high. Actual number will be more like 6 to 8.” The count matters because Starship burns nearly all of its propellant just reaching orbit. SpaceX’s plan is to launch a depot ship, fill it with a string of tanker launches and then send the lander up to fuel before it heads for the Moon. Every tanker trip is a full rocket launch, adding time, cost and risk before a crew ever leaves Earth.

stories.headline: Trumbull’s Kids Pumpkin Fest is Sunday on the Town Hall Green with pumpkin decorating, a live DJ and touch-a-truck
stories.summary: Trumbull’s annual Kids Pumpkin Fest runs this Sunday, Oct. 25, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on the Town Hall Green at 5866 Main Street, Patch reports. The free family event features pumpkin decorating, face painting, lawn games, crafts and a live DJ, plus a touch-a-truck with the Long Hill Fire and Trumbull Police departments and crafts with the Trumbull Nature and Arts Center. Mobile coffee trailer Brewberry Cafe will serve a seasonal menu.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: a hearing on a one-year data center moratorium, early voting opens Monday at the library, and a Town Hall Halloween parade
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Planning and Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing Wednesday on a proposed text amendment that would define data centers as their own principal use in the town’s zoning rules and put a one-year moratorium on them, according to the meeting agenda, Patch reports in its weekly look at what’s coming up in town. Early voting for the Nov. 3 election runs Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, at the Trumbull Library, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk. Patch also points to First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s statement on the proposed high-density housing development at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe, near the Coventry Lane area of Trumbull; no application is pending in Trumbull, and residents can send comments to the Monroe Planning and Zoning Commission. The Commission on Aging will hear an update on fraud prevention and a Senior Center report, and preschoolers can trick-or-treat through Town Hall in the annual Halloween parade, which has two sessions of 20 children each and requires registration.
